annotations.title: Symptoms & Causes of Urinary Retention - NIDDK
Symptoms & Causes of Urinary Retention - NIDDK

content.text:
A bladder that doesn’t empty fully is called **urinary retention**. It usually happens for one of two reasons: **something is blocking urine flow**, or **the bladder muscle/nerves aren’t working well enough to push urine out**. ([niddk.nih.gov](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/urinary-retention/symptoms-causes?utm_source=openai))

Common causes include:

- **Enlarged prostate** in men, which can squeeze the urethra and slow/block flow.
- **Urinary tract infection (UTI)** or inflammation, which can cause swelling or pain that interferes with urination.
- **Constipation**, because a full rectum can press on the bladder/urethra.
- **Certain medications**, especially some antihistamines, decongestants, antidepressants, opioids, muscle relaxers, and bladder-control medicines.
- **Nerve problems** from diabetes, stroke, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, spinal injury, or pelvic surgery.
- **Weak bladder muscle / underactive bladder**, sometimes from aging, long-term overdistension, diabetes, or nerve issues.
- **Urethral stricture/scarring**, bladder stones, tumors, or pelvic organ prolapse.
- **After surgery or anesthesia**, which can temporarily make it hard to urinate.

**Get urgent medical care now** if you **can’t pee at all**, have severe lower belly pain/swelling, fever, back/flank pain, vomiting, new leg weakness/numbness, or blood in the urine. Acute urinary retention can be an emergency. ([niddk.nih.gov](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/urinary-retention/symptoms-causes?utm_source=openai))

If this is ongoing—weak stream, stopping/starting, feeling not empty, frequent urination, leaking, or waking often to pee—it’s worth seeing a clinician/urologist. They can check for retained urine with a quick bladder scan and look for causes like UTI, prostate enlargement, medication effects, or nerve/bladder muscle problems.
